ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, directors, and beneficial owners against the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the European Union consolidated sanctions list, and the Hong Kong Police Force's Counter-Terrorism and Organized Crime lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for any individual or entity appearing on any list, including source of funds verification, adverse media checks, and ongoing transaction monitoring. The screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a real-time basis for new sanctions, and annually for existing relationships. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Business Registration Office (BRO) of the Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in English, Chinese, or both. English names must be in Latin script; Chinese names must be in Traditional Chinese characters. Phonetic transliteration is permitted but must be consistent with the official pronunciation. The four-tier naming convention assesses (1) exact match, (2) phonetic similarity, (3) visual similarity, and (4) conceptual similarity against existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written appeal to the Business Registration Office within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a legal declaration explaining the distinctiveness of the proposed name, a copy of the rejection letter, and a non-refundable fee of HKD 200. The BRO will review the appeal within 21 working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of Hong Kong within 28 days of the denial. The entire process typically takes 60-90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mailbox services are permissible for registration purposes, but the Inland Revenue Department and banks may require a physical presence for AML and tax compliance. For a low-risk MMORPG publishing business with global operations, a virtual office is acceptable if a local agent is appointed and all records are accessible. However, banks may reject virtual offices for high-risk transactions; given the low-risk tier, it is likely acceptable, but a physical office is recommended to mitigate any potential scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Verify that the registered address is a valid physical location; (2) Ensure the nameplate is displayed; (3) Maintain complete business records and contracts; (4) Have a local representative available during business hours. Risk: Low to moderate, with an estimated 10% probability of an unannounced inspection by the Inland Revenue Department or the Companies Registry within the first year of operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) of the Laws of Hong Kong, particularly sections 5 (registration), 6 (name and statement), 7 (certificate of registration), and 8 (effect of registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong, Limited Partnership Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statement of Limited Partnership (Form LP1) together with the executed Partnership Agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong limited partnerships have no statutory minimum capital requirement. Capital contributions are determined solely by the partnership agreement and may be in cash, property, or services. No escrow or blocked account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [PARTNERSHIP NAME] (THE 'PARTNERSHIP') ADOPTED BY WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE]. WHEREAS, the Partnership is a limited partnership formed under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) of Hong Kong; and WHEREAS, the General Partner is authorized to manage the affairs of the Partnership and to execute all documents and take all actions necessary to effectuate the formation and operational commencement of the Partnership; NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. That the Partnership Agreement, as presented to the General Partner, is hereby approved, adopted, and ratified in its entirety, and the General Partner is authorized to execute and deliver the same to the Companies Registry as part of the registration filing. 2. That the initial capital contributions of the partners, as set forth in the Partnership Agreement, are hereby subscribed and accepted, and the General Partner is directed to cause the receipt and recording of such contributions in the Partnership's books and records. 3. That the registered office of the Partnership shall be established at [Address], Hong Kong, and the General Partner is authorized to engage a registered office service provider if necessary, and to file the required notice with the Companies Registry. 4. That the General Partner is hereby authorized to open and maintain one or more bank accounts in the name of the Partnership with [Bank Name], and to designate the authorized signatories, including the General Partner and any appointed officers, with full authority to deposit, withdraw, and manage funds in accordance with the Partnership Agreement. 5. That the following persons are hereby appointed as statutory officers of the Partnership: [Name] as Compliance Officer, [Name] as Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO), and [Name] as Secretary, each to serve until resignation or removal by the General Partner. 6. That the General Partner is authorized to execute all documents, file all forms, and take all steps necessary to obtain the Certificate of Registration from the Companies Registry, to register with the Inland Revenue Department for business registration, and to comply with all applicable laws and regulations. 7. That the General Partner is authorized to engage legal counsel, accountants, and other professional advisors as may be required to ensure full compliance with Hong Kong law and to facilitate the global operations of the Partnership. 8. That any actions taken prior to the date of this resolution in furtherance of the formation of the Partnership are hereby ratified and confirmed. This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force and effect until revoked or amended by a subsequent resolution of the General Partner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong – Online Name Search and Reservation System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search on the Companies Registry's Cyber Search Centre to ensure the proposed partnership name is not identical or too similar to an existing entity. If the name is available, file an application for name reservation (Form NNC1 for companies, but for limited partnerships, the name is reserved as part of the registration application; however, a separate name reservation is not mandatory). Verify that the name does not contain prohibited words (e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust') without prior consent. Prepare the proposed name in both English and Chinese (if desired) and ensure it ends with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' as required by the Limited Partnership Ordinance. Submit the name reservation request online or in person, paying the applicable fee (HKD 1,430 for registration, which includes name approval). Await confirmation of name availability and reservation, which typically takes 1-2 business days.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all general partners (passport or HKID)
Proof of address of general partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or prohibited words, the applicant will receive a notice from the Companies Registry. The applicant may file an objection or amend the name and resubmit. Alternatively, the applicant may seek consent from the existing entity or apply for a name change. The remedy is to revise the name and re-file, with no additional fee if done within 14 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Not applicable – internal drafting by legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Hong Kong-licensed attorney to draft a comprehensive Partnership Agreement that complies with the Limited Partnership Ordinance and the specific needs of the foreign-invested partnership. The agreement must specify the name, nature of business, duration, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, management rights, and the roles of general and limited partners. It must also include provisions for admission and withdrawal of partners, dispute resolution, and dissolution. The agreement must be executed by all partners, with signatures witnessed by a notary public or other authorized person. Ensure that the agreement is executed in both English and Chinese (if required) and that each partner receives a certified copy. The executed agreement will be submitted to the Companies Registry as part of the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of all partners
Power of attorney if any partner is represented
Notarized copies of corporate partners' incorporation documents (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry queries the agreement for non-compliance, the attorney will revise the agreement to address the specific objections. The partners must execute the amended version. If the agreement is rejected due to missing information, the registry will issue a notice; the applicant has 14 days to cure the deficiency by submitting the required documents or amendments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong – Limited Partnership Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Statement of Limited Partnership (Form LP1) along with the executed Partnership Agreement and the prescribed fee (HKD 1,430) with the Companies Registry. The form must be signed by all general partners and include the partnership name, registered office address, nature of business, and details of partners (name, address, and contribution). Submit the application online via the e-Registry portal or in person at the Companies Registry counter. The Registry will review the application for completeness and compliance with the Limited Partnership Ordinance. Upon approval, the Registry will issue a Certificate of Registration. The entire process typically takes 5-7 business days. After registration, the partnership must file a copy of the certificate with the Inland Revenue Department for business registration.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (e.g., lease agreement or service provider confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or queried, the Registry will issue a notice specifying the deficiencies. The applicant must respond within 14 days by providing the missing information or correcting errors. If the issue is substantive (e.g., illegal business purpose), the applicant may need to amend the partnership agreement and resubmit. If the application is rejected, the applicant may appeal to the Companies Registry's Review Board or seek judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department – Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the Certificate of Registration, apply for a Business Registration Certificate from the Inland Revenue Department. Submit the completed Form IRBR1 (Application for Business Registration) along with a copy of the Certificate of Registration and the prescribed fee (HKD 2,000 per year). The Business Registration Certificate must be displayed at the registered office. Additionally, the partnership must appoint a Compliance Officer and an AML/CFT Officer as per the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) if the partnership engages in regulated activities. For a software publishing business, this may not be mandatory, but it is prudent to have a compliance framework. The partnership must also open a corporate bank account with a licensed bank, providing the Certificate of Registration, Business Registration Certificate, and the Partnership Agreement. Finally, the partnership must file annual returns with the Companies Registry (if required) and maintain proper accounting records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration from Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration application is delayed or rejected, the partnership may contact the Business Registration Office for clarification. Common issues include incomplete forms or incorrect fee payment. The remedy is to correct the form and resubmit. If the partnership fails to register within the statutory period, a late fee may be imposed; the partnership can apply for a waiver if the delay was due to reasonable cause.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – the business is purely digital (software publishing) and does not involve physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – no physical premises or industrial operations; only a registered office and virtual operations. No fire safety certification, structural load inspections, or workplace safety approvals are required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; electronic portal: eTax (https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/etax.htm)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a partnership, the entity itself does not obtain a separate Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN); instead, each partner must have a TIN (for individuals: Hong Kong Identity Card number or passport number; for corporations: Business Registration Number). The partnership must register for a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) within one month of commencement of business. The application is made via Form IRBR 1 (Business Registration Application) to the Business Registration Office of the IRD. For non-resident partners, they must apply for a TIN from the IRD by submitting a completed Form IR 1121 (Application for Taxpayer Identification Number) along with supporting documents such as passport copy and proof of address. The partnership must provide details of all partners and their profit-sharing ratios. Upon approval, the partnership receives a Business Registration Certificate with a Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the primary tax identifier for the partnership. Each partner's TIN is then used for individual tax assessment under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong does not offer check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections. Partnerships are automatically treated as pass-through entities; profits are allocated to partners and taxed at the partner level under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST (Hong Kong operates a territorial-based profits tax system; no indirect tax on goods or services)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable. Hong Kong does not mandate electronic invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance for indirect tax purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Hong Kong does not impose VAT or GST on exports; therefore, there is no zero-rating claim mechanism. Exports of goods and services are outside the scope of Hong Kong profits tax if the profits arise outside Hong Kong (territorial source principle). For goods, exports are not subject to any indirect tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration (if required by the Trade and Industry Department)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Not applicable for VAT. However, for profits tax, if a taxpayer incorrectly claims offshore sourcing or fails to report income, penalties under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) may apply, including additional tax assessments up to 100% of tax underpaid and potential prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) with delegated enforcement authority to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the PRC Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations, the RMB is fully convertible for current account items, including cross-border trade in services and software royalties, subject to genuine transaction verification. Capital account transactions remain strictly controlled; foreign direct investment (FDI) into a Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) requires SAFE registration and a dedicated capital account. Profit remittance by the FIP to overseas partners is permissible only after submission of audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, and a SAFE-designated bank verification. Additionally, the 'surrender and settlement' mechanism has been replaced by a 'foreign currency retention' system, allowing companies to retain export proceeds in foreign currency or convert at their discretion, provided the underlying transaction is bona fide. Special attention is required for cross-border digital game revenue derived from App Store/Google Play payouts, which must be classified under current account service trade codes (e.g., 228020) and substantiated with platform payout statements. The offshore RMB (CNH) market in Hong Kong remains segregated from the onshore CNY market, and any capital flow between them is subject to macro-prudential limits and cross-border financing rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: PRC rules do not require mandatory conversion of export proceeds into CNY; the previous surrender requirements were abolished effective 2001. Nevertheless, all cross-border FX receipts must be repatriated to a designated domestic bank account within 6 months of the transaction date and registered with the SAFE-in-licensed bank no later than 5 business days after receipt. The conversion ratio is at the enterprise's discretion, but any conversion exceeding USD 50,000 equivalent requires underlying contract and tax documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI solutions such as Revolut Business, Wise, or Airwallex are legally prohibited from providing multi-currency business accounts or payment services to onshore PRC entities. Only licensed commercial banks and qualified payment institutions approved by PBOC and SAFE can operate FX settlement and clearing. Offshore EMIs may, however, serve the Hong Kong SAR treasury function if a parallel HK entity is established, but not for the CN-FIP itself. Therefore, the viability of fintech EMI for the onshore FIP is rated 'Nil' for treasury accounts; they can only be used for employee expense cards or procurement in limited jurisdictions with no FX conversion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the current PRC KYC and anti-money laundering regime (Law on Anti-Money Laundering 2019), at least one natural person designated as the FIP's executive partner or an authorized signatory holding a certified power of attorney must appear physically at the bank branch for an interview. Remote opening is not permitted for foreign-invested partnerships unless the individual is in mainland China and completes a video verification at a notary office. Consular proxy opening is allowed for foreign partners, provided the power of attorney is notarized at the Chinese embassy/consulate and authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, followed by an in-branch video interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity of foreign partners in a multi-tiered offshore holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry certificates and certificate of incumbency for each entity level; notarized beneficial ownership declaration form (updated within 90 days); organisational chart endorsed by the partnership's legal counsel; and source-of-funds evidence (bank statements of investing partners for the last 12 months) to evidence legitimate wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction tainting due to MMORPG global distribution covering sanctioned or high-risk territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Geo-blocking policy and IP reputation-enforcement documentation; a copy of the third-party sanctions screening software log; a record of denied-party list checks for the past 12 months; and a clear operational undertaking that no in-game virtual currency can be converted to fiat currency outside licensed exchanges.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between reported revenue and platform payout cycles, creating unrealised FX exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple App Store and Google Play monthly payout statements for 6 months with unique order IDs; bank transaction history of the settlement account showing all inbound wires; accounting reconciliation signed by a PRC CPA; and tax compliance filings including VAT and income tax returns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential use of the partnership for trade-based money laundering through over/under-invoicing of software licences
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original software licensing agreements with overseas distributors; detailed royalty calculation methodology; transfer pricing documentation compliant with BEPS actions; and independent audit confirmation of the arm's-length pricing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For injecting foreign direct investment into the CN FIP, the following compliant route applies: (1) Register FDI with SAFE through the designated bank (FDI Foreign Exchange Registration); (2) Open a Capital Account (FDI) to receive inbound wire remittances from the overseas partner, with the remittance purpose coded as 'Equity Injection for Establishment of FIP' under current SAFE codes (e.g., 601); (3) Upon each inward remittance, the bank verifies the registration certificate, the amount being within the total inscribed capital, and requires a 'Payment Use Letter' for any within-CNY re-conversion; (4) After settlement into CNY, the funds must be credited to a separate RMB basic settlement account and used strictly for the partnership's business operations; capital verification by a local CPA must be completed within 30 days. Inbound shareholder loans also require a 'Foreign Debt' quota registration and may be converted into CNY under the national macro-prudential policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from the FIP for trade in services (such as software royalties, server hosting, marketing, and administrative fees) are processed through the current account. The company must submit an 'Application for Settlement and Sale of Foreign Exchange' with supporting documents: commercial contract, invoice, tax certificate evidence for royalties, and a non-trade outbound payment tax filing (for remittances > USD 50,000). The preferred clearing rails are: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers; (b) Standby Letters of Credit for contractual royalties; (c) documentary collections for peer-to-peer transactions. All MT103 messages must include the proper purpose code (e.g., '228030 Software Payments'), and the bank's compliance team screens the beneficiary against sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CNY forward settlement and sale contracts (with real trade background)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for foreign-currency debt

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month before the expiry of the current Business Registration Certificate, being the annual anniversary of the original registration date; renewal must be completed annually before the stated expiry date on the BRC.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a statutory penalty of HKD 300 where the certificate is less than one month overdue and HKD 1,500 where the certificate is more than one month overdue; continued default may lead to prosecution, a fine not exceeding HKD 5,000, daily default fines, and suspension or administrative revocation of the business registration, rendering the partnership unable to legally carry on business in Hong Kong.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Return (prescribed annual return of the limited partnership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Registrar of Companies, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary date of registration of the limited partnership, for every year following execution and registration of the limited partnership deed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Every general partner in default is liable to a fine of HKD 50 for each day the default continues; the Registrar may also initiate administrative strike-off proceedings against the limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance, with costs and restoration penalties applied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for a Partnership (Form BIR52)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR, Assessment Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month from the date of issue of the return; for accounting periods ending on 31 December, an automatic one-month extension is generally granted by IRD, with an additional two-month extension made available for electronic filing via e-Tax, bringing the final effective deadline to approximately 30 June for the lax return year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse exposes the partnerships and its partners to estimated assessments levied on the taxable profits, late payment interest at the prevailing judgment rate (currently 8% per annum), and additional penalties under the Inland Revenue Ordinance up to 200% of the undercharged tax, including prosecution for deliberate non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employers' Return (Form BIR56A and Individual Employee Remuneration Tables BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR, Central Processing Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued annually on or around 1 April; the return must be submitted to the IRD within one month of the date of issue, unless an extension has been requested and granted in writing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An employer failing without reasonable excuse to furnish the Employers' Return is liable to a fine of HKD 10,000 plus a daily default fine of HKD 1,000 per day; the IRD may also claim a penalty of up to three times the amount of tax or additional tax assessed as evaded.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary Hong Kong partnership is not automatically subject to a statutory audit under the Partnership Ordinance or the Companies Ordinance; however, an independent audit becomes compulsory if (i) the partnership is required by the terms of its financial institution lending, private equity or group reporting covenants to produce independently audited financial statements; (ii) the partnership is elected or structured as a Hong Kong private company or limited liability vehicle under the Companies Ordinance and fails the 'small private company' exemption; or (iii) the partnership is a Licensed Corporation or a financial institution regulated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority or Securities and Futures Commission. For a Hong Kong private company, the exemptions apply only where the entity satisfies at least two of the three micro-enterprise thresholds prescribed under the Companies Ordinance Cap. 622: annual total revenue not exceeding HKD 10 million, year-end total assets not exceeding HKD 10 million, and not more than 50 employees. When the statutory audit is required, the audit must be conducted by a Hong Kong Certified Public Accountant (Practising) under Part 9 of the Accounting and Financial Reporting Council Ordinance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) as issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants, which are substantially identical to International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); the HKFRS for Private Entities is permissible for eligible private partnerships that do not carry on a business as a public accountability entity, and the applicable framework for tax filing is the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Ordinance and Hong Kong accounting principles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not maintain a statutory central UBO registry for ordinary foreign-invested partnerships. However, the partnership must comply with the Significant Controllers Register regime only if the vehicle is a Hong Kong company; for a Hong Kong limited partnership, any change in the identity, shareholding interest, capital contribution, or participation ratio of any partner must be reported to the Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office and, where applicable, the Companies Registry, within 30 days of the change. The same 30-day reporting window applies to transfers of partnership interests and changes in the composition of general or limited partners. As a compliance best practice, the partnership should hold an annual UBO confirmation exercise to update its internal beneficial ownership matrix, file notices of change with the Business Registration Office on a 30-day event-driven basis, and maintain the latest ownership schedule at the registered office for inspection.

Register of Charges or Mortgages over partnership assets

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,300 per annum for a compliant Hong Kong registered office, licensed corporate secretarial or partnership agent, and virtual office arrangement for a foreign-invested partnership.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 9,000 for a reasonable-scope independent CPA audit of a typical non-listed Hong Kong partnership holding MMORPG royalty and platform payout streams; USD 9,000 - USD 25,000 for a group-consolidated audit with intercompany licensing and app-store revenue recognition.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% for a Hong Kong Foreign-Invested Partnership treated as an unincorporated business; a corporate general partner is assessable at 16.5%, subject to the two-tiered profits tax rates
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Hong Kong applies a territorial source principle: offshore-sourced profits are outside the scope of profits tax. Two-tiered concessions apply: 7.5% for the first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profits for unincorporated businesses and 8.25% for corporations, with the excess taxed at 15% or 16.5% respectively. Additional incentives include 100% deduction for capital expenditure on prescribed intellectual property rights, enhanced R&D super-deductions of 300%/200% on qualifying expenditure up to HKD 20,000,000, profits tax exemption for qualifying offshore funds, no capital gains tax, and no statutory withholding tax on dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return Form BIR52 (Partnership) under the Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap. 112, filed with the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department (IRD) via the eTAX electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IRD issues the BIR52 annually; for a standard 31 March fiscal year-end the return is issued in April and is due within 1 month (normally 2 May), or within 3 months for tax representatives (customarily extended to 15 August). A non-resident partner may apply for a further extension only with substantive justification acceptable to the IRD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Business Registration Number and Partner Identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the FIP's Business Registration Number under the Business Registration Ordinance, full legal name, and particulars of all partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Foreign-Invested Partnership with non-resident partners, state each partner's overseas registration or tax identification number and country of tax residence. Retain the partnership deed, constitutional documents, and the non-resident partners' Tax Residency Certificates for declaration and audit verification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Principal Business Activity and Place of Central Management and Control
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Describe the principal trade as ISIC 5820 publishing of hardcore MMORPG games with Apple App Store and Google Play in-app purchase revenue; confirm the address of the partnership's principal place of business in Hong Kong
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a portion of profit is claimed as offshore-sourced, this box must cross-reference a detailed offshore profit schedule evidencing where game development, contract execution, server management, and monetisation decisions occur. The IRD will examine whether central management and control is genuinely in Hong Kong; a bare booking office with no senior staff will be fatal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the accounting reference date and the period from the first day to the last day covered by the return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accounts must be prepared under Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards or equivalent. All non-HKD receipts from Apple App Store and Google Play settlement statements must be translated into HKD at a consistent and acceptable exchange rate, with exchange gains or losses classified in accordance with IRD practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross proceeds from all MMORPG digital sales, in-app purchases, subscriptions, and royalties, excluding only those profits separately claimed and substantiated as offshore-sourced
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate platform payouts net of commissions and refunds, and reconcile the figure with merchant settlement reports. Non-resident partners must identify any Hong Kong dependent agent or permanent establishment; the absence of a PE merely because the FIP is pass-through will not automatically protect non-resident partners where the FIP is managed and controlled in Hong Kong.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Allowable Deductions and Capital Allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List deductible expenses such as server hosting, bandwidth, third-party development costs, marketing, rent, salaries, licensing fees, and capital allowances for software and relevant fixed assets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in producing assessable profits are deductible; partnership distributions to partners are never deductible. Non-resident partners may not deduct head-office or overseas general and administrative expenses unless they directly support Hong Kong-sourced income and are evidenced by contemporaneous invoices and contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Adjusted Assessable Profit / Adjusted Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute aggregate assessable profit/(loss) after deducting allowable expenses and adding back non-deductible items and transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box forms the partnership level aggregate figure before allocation. If a loss is declared, detail the loss carry-forward computations and, for non-resident partners, confirm that any loss is not attributable to tax-exempt offshore activities. Transfer pricing adjustments under the arm's length principle must be made before allocation to non-resident partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Allocation of Assessable Profit / Loss among Partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Set out each partner's share ratio and the apportioned assessable profit or loss in accordance with the partnership agreement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter full identification details for each non-resident partner and state whether the allocated income is effectively connected with a Hong Kong permanent establishment. If treaty relief is sought, attach a statement of beneficial ownership and the Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate; a non-resident partner claiming reduced source taxation must ensure the relevant Double Tax Arrangement is applicable and the principal purpose test is satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Tax Representative Declaration and Signature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The person in charge of the FIP's affairs or an appointed authorised tax representative must sign and certify the contents of the return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Foreign-Invested Partnership with all partners resident outside Hong Kong, appoint a Hong Kong tax representative and attach the formal authorisation. An unsigned or incomplete declaration will be treated as an invalid return and may trigger penalties; the signatory must attest to the accuracy of all non-resident schedules, PE analysis, offshore profit claims, and treaty relief documentations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the Profits Tax Return without reasonable excuse attracts a fine of HKD 10,000 under section 80(2) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance plus an additional daily penalty not exceeding HKD 1,000 per day of default. Where a return is knowingly false or contains a materially misleading statement with intent to evade tax, conviction on indictment exposes the FIP to a fine of HKD 100,000 and imprisonment for 3 years under section 82, with additional tax under section 82A of up to three times the amount of tax undercharged.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% statutory dividend withholding tax in Hong Kong; however, where a Chinese-source distribution is made from a mainland enterprise or partnership to a Hong Kong partner, the PRC dividend withholding tax is 10% under domestic law, reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement if the Hong Kong beneficial owner holds at least 25% of the enterprise for 12 months before the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the Hong Kong resident partner must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate from the IRD using Form IR1314A and pay the HKD 500 application fee. The partner must complete a beneficial ownership declaration, hold not less than 25% equity interest for an uninterrupted 12-month period, satisfy the PRC anti-abuse rules under SAT Announcement [2018] No. 9, and demonstrate genuine economic substance in Hong Kong, including substantive decision-making for the MMORPG business. The Chinese payer must file the withholding return within 7 days of the distribution, attach the Tax Residency Certificate, obtain the reduced-rate approval (or unilateral domestic procedural treaty claim), remit the 5% withholding tax, and retain the tax payment certificate, partnership agreement, platform settlement records, and evidence of beneficial ownership for at least 10 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Hong Kong does not impose a statutory withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents. Royalties paid for the use of intellectual property in Hong Kong are deemed assessable profits of a non-resident person, producing an effective Hong Kong profits tax cost of approximately 4.95% (15% unincorporated rate applied to a deemed 30% gross royalty margin) or 4.95%/5.17% depending on entity status, absent treaty protection. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong Arrangement, interest and royalties sourced in China and paid to a Hong Kong beneficial owner are limited to 7% withholding (compared with up to 10% domestic withholding), subject to the filing of the appropriate non-resident withholding forms, certification of residence, and satisfaction of the beneficial ownership and principal purpose tests.
